mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% indicates tightening monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising housing starts (HOUST) and strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST and RSAFS are rising.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when INDPRO rises.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation environments (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), strong GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates economic resilience that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and GDPC1 growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) typically leads to tighter monetary policy, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises.
